title: One Call Property Solutions vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: Landlords and managers comparing One Call Property Solutions with Precision Paint Experts: what to ask about rental turnover painting, scope, and paperwork.
h1: One Call Property Solutions vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Rental turnovers run on tight calendars. This page covers the questions property owners and managers should ask any painter before a unit goes back on the market.

questions: How fast can a rental unit be repainted between tenants?
What insurance paperwork should a property manager get from a painter?

body: Owners and managers sometimes get a bid from One Call Property Solutions and another from Precision Paint Experts for the same units. Describing another vendor's services isn't something we'll do. Our aim here is narrower: to lay out the factors that drive rental turnover painting, so every vendor answers the same list.

Turnover work is about predictability. Vacancy days cost money, and the unit has to look clean and consistent enough to photograph and show. The painter's paperwork and scheduling matter as much as their brushwork.

sections.h2: What to confirm before the first unit
body: Ask each vendor for answers to these, ideally before you need them in a hurry:
bullets: Will you issue an insurance certificate listing our company before the first unit?
Is every crew member covered by workers' comp?
Are the crews your own, or subcontracted?
What product and sheen go on walls, trim, and doors, so maintenance can match them later?
How are drywall dings, nail pops, and patches handled and priced?

body: Florida licensing, bonding, and full insurance are all in place, workers' comp covers each painter we send, and your management company or LLC can receive an insurance certificate in its name before the crew mobilizes. Every painter at your property is our employee; turnover work is never subbed out.

In a vacant unit, plan on roughly one day per room, while repainting an entire unit or house takes three days to two weeks, driven by its size and how it was left. Dings and holes in the walls go through our drywall repair and patching service, and the quote spells out which surfaces are in scope, closets and ceilings included or not, so nobody argues about it later. Bigger portfolios are a fit for our multi-family and apartment painting and property management painting work.

Communication matters just as much on a smooth turnover. The written schedule tells your leasing team when a unit will be ready to show, and because nothing is added later without written approval, you will not find surprise line items when the invoice arrives. If a crew discovers damage that was hidden behind furniture or appliances, it is documented and sent to you for a decision before any extra work happens.

One way to cut turnover time is to pick one wall color, one trim color, and one sheen for all units, recorded on the estimate by product line. That makes touch-ups faster, and the labelled leftover cans we hand over let maintenance staff fix small scuffs between full repaints. Low-VOC options help when neighboring units are occupied.
To see which sheens wipe clean best in busy rentals, read our article on picking the right paint finish.

A crew lead can usually walk your unit within 48 hours, and a line-item quote tends to land about a business day afterward. Request a free estimate for one unit or a batch of them, and put it next to whatever other bids you're holding.
For a portfolio spread across several towns, our five counties take in Gainesville, Ocala, Lake City, and the smaller towns between them, so a single vendor can cover units in different places.

faqs.q: Will you list our LLC by name on your insurance certificate?
faqs.a: Yes. For property managers, HOAs, and commercial clients, we issue a certificate naming your entity before the crew mobilizes.

faqs.q: How many days to repaint a vacant rental?
faqs.a: Usually about a day per room. An entire unit or house takes three days to two weeks, depending on its size, its condition, and the repairs needed.

faqs.q: Do you use subcontractors on rental jobs?
faqs.a: No. Rental units are painted by our own employees, and we never subcontract a turnover.
